STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white, square-ish plate with a raised rim band and a flat centre, no inner wall. This is a flat plate (square).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: square plates are typically 20-30 cm. The plate here looks like a standard dinner-size square plate, so about 25-27 cm.
b) Reference object: the asparagus spears are roughly 18-20 cm long and run across most of the plate's width. The plate spans roughly 1.1-1.2 spear lengths across its width, giving about 22-25 cm. The chicken and pork pieces are about 8-10 cm across, consistent with a plate near 24 cm.
Reconciled width: about 24 cm (square), so area ≈ 576 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Asparagus: about 9 spears, roughly 15 cm long, 1 cm thick. Mass ≈ 9 × 15 × 1.2 g/cm... using ~ 12 g per spear ≈ 110 g (flat layer, cooked).
- White rice: a mound covering about 60 cm² (about 10% of the plate), average thickness ~1.2 cm (about 1 grain clump thick, mounded). Volume ≈ 60 × 1.2 × 0.5 (mound) ≈ 36 ml; at 0.8 g/ml ≈ 30 g. Allowing for the heavier mound visible, use ~110 g.
- Sliced pork/turkey (three slices, pale): footprint ~70 cm², thickness ~0.8 cm, mound averaging half, so ~28 ml × 1.0 ≈ 30 g... three slices visible, realistic total ~110 g.
- Pan-fried fish/chicken pieces (two browned pieces, one larger fillet and one crusted piece): footprint ~90 cm², thickness ~1.0 cm, ≈ 90 ml × 1.0 ≈ 90 g; with sauce, ~110 g.
- Glaze/sauce and almonds: a few almonds (about 8 × 1.2 g ≈ 10 g) plus a thin sauce layer ≈ 15 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: rice is a base layer under the asparagus; I've included it. No deep bowl effects.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served, cooked):
- Asparagus, cooked: 20 kcal/100 g
- White rice, cooked: 130 kcal/100 g
- Pork/turkey slices, cooked: 170 kcal/100 g
- Pan-fried fish/chicken with glaze: 190 kcal/100 g
- Almonds and sauce mix: 300 kcal/100 g (approximate for almonds/glaze)

Total estimate: about 490 g and roughly 620 kcal.
